policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the name 'Hiram', which transliterates the ketiv חירם (with yod, i-vowel); the qere חוּרָם (with waw, u-vowel) would yield 'Huram'. The English spelling distinguishes the readings and follows the ketiv.

Qere פְּלִשְׁתִּים and ketiv פלשתיים differ only in plene spelling of the plural; both are rendered 'the Philistines'. ASV wording, supplies, and notes give nothing to distinguish them; base fallback retained.
